cases.name: already-complete
cases.why: Every marker is present and the skeleton equals the template. Today's behaviour, and it must stay byte-for-byte identical.

cases.name: empty-file
cases.why: A zero-byte authorized file halts today, and both diagnoses the error offers are false. An empty file has nothing to destroy, which is the reason Phase 3 is create-if-absent at all.

cases.name: rails-new-routes
cases.why: The motivating case. The expected output is byte-identical to what prov-2026-ee1b3e46 plants by hand in a Ruby target script, which is the thing this record exists to stop needing.

cases.name: rails-generate-bare
cases.source: `rails generate controller Todos`, rendered from railties' own controller.rb.tt
cases.why: The whole template body lands and the result equals the rendered template. Note the file's bare `end` matches the class's closing line and not the rescue block's `  end`: indentation is compared, and normalising it would place this wrongly rather than fail.

cases.name: rails-generate-actions
cases.diagnostic: replace at file line 2, replace at file line 5
cases.why: The hand-written def index and def show are exactly what createControllerMethod injects into the actions region. Whether they should become owned regions is a question Sedum cannot answer, so it must not guess.

cases.name: private-empty
cases.why: The file's own private keyword is reused rather than duplicated: the rescue block and the actions anchor go above it, the private anchor below. 'Insert it into any file that does not already have one' falls out of the diff instead of being a rule.

cases.name: private-with-method
cases.why: Refused because of def set_todo, not because of private. The distinction matters: a file may carry the template's structure, but not body content the template has no counterpart for.

cases.name: evolution-anchor-and-code
cases.why: A file an earlier run generated, whose template has since gained a private section and an anchor. Both are inserted below the existing injected region, so the method already there stays public. This is the case that has no answer at all today.

cases.name: evolution-bare-anchor
cases.why: The same, where the template gained only an anchor. It lands in position rather than at the end of the class, which is what fails if the skeleton is aligned without its markers.

cases.name: edited-boilerplate
cases.why: Someone changed the superclass of a generated file. The template is no longer a description of it, and reconciling would overwrite a decision a person made.

cases.name: default-template
cases.why: A _default template is one marker and nothing else, so it shares no structure with any real file. The low-structure case refuses itself rather than needing a rule against it.
